_comment: Terminal > Run Task > 'Atlas: ...'. Every report lands in work/ as UTF-8 (never use the shell's '>' - PowerShell 5.1 writes UTF-16). The /atlas-* chat prompts in .github/prompts read these files.

inputs.description: Program / job / PROC / copybook / transaction / field name
What NAME is (when the index cannot tell, e.g. a PSB and a job share the program's name)
Pack budget in characters (about 4 characters per token)
Field name (copybook name or the program's REPLACING name; an 88 name works too)
Second field for the cross-field rules (repeat the first if there is none)
Message-text pattern, e.g. GENDER or INVALID REL
Literal / error / status code, e.g. E001
Member name (a program, copybook, job, PROC, PSB, DBD, control card...)
Document name (the file name without extension, as `docs` shows it)
Line range, e.g. 1-9999 for the whole member or 120-180
Paragraph / section name, or a line number
The production copy: SYSTEM/NAME (GC/CLMPOST), NAME@LIBRARY, a path, or just NAME when the index holds two copies
The changed copy: SYSTEM/NAME (GC-TEST/CLMPOST), NAME@LIBRARY, or the path of the downloaded file; leave blank to take the other copy in the index
System folder holding the changed copies (e.g. GC-TEST); blank = every member whose copies differ

tasks.label: Atlas: pack NAME -> work/pack.md
tasks.detail: The dossier plus the evidence lines, inside a budget. Kind is detected (program, job, copybook, transaction, field).

tasks.label: Atlas: pack NAME (choose kind) -> work/pack.md
tasks.detail: Same, but you say what NAME is - needed when a PSB or a job shares a program's name.

tasks.label: Atlas: walk PROGRAM -> work/walk.md
tasks.detail: The program in reading order: entry first, each paragraph as control reaches it, resolved facts, source, the data it touches. For 'what does this program do'.

tasks.label: Atlas: diff OLD NEW -> work/diff.md
tasks.detail: Two versions of a member - the production copy and the changed one: the paragraphs, calls, copybooks, tables, files and fields that changed (fields that only shifted are grouped), then the changed lines of both sides with their own numbers, citable.

tasks.label: Atlas: release contents -> work/release.md
tasks.detail: Every member that exists in two libraries with different content (production vs the changed copies), with the diff command for each, and members new to the test system.

tasks.label: Atlas: whole member -> work/cite.md
tasks.detail: Numbered source lines of one member (default: all of it). For 'explain this program' and for checking a citation.

tasks.label: Atlas: paragraph -> work/paragraph.md
tasks.detail: One paragraph or section: who reaches it, what it does, its source.

tasks.label: Atlas: field -> work/field.md
tasks.detail: Every definition (offset, length, skew), every program, every reference by mode, 88 values, sort cards on its bytes.

tasks.label: Atlas: layout -> work/layout.md
tasks.detail: Byte layout of a copybook (record length on top) - for test data and interface contracts.

tasks.label: Atlas: literal / error code -> work/literal.md
tasks.detail: Where a code is defined, set, tested, displayed, and where the value flows afterwards.

tasks.label: Atlas: job -> work/job.md
tasks.detail: Effective steps (PROCs expanded), control cards quoted, datasets with direction, guards, INTRDR submits.

tasks.label: Atlas: crud for a job -> work/crud.md
tasks.detail: Create / Read / Update / Delete per program against datasets, tables, IMS databases, CICS files.

tasks.label: Atlas: conditions -> work/conditions.md
tasks.detail: Every IF / WHEN / sort INCLUDE-OMIT test in a program with its values - the test-condition inventory.

tasks.label: Atlas: value domain (values + pair + messages + field) -> work/
tasks.detail: For a value-domain change: work/values.md, work/pair.md, work/messages.md, work/field.md in one go.
tasks.command: python -m atlas.query --db atlas.db --out work/values.md values ${input:field}; python -m atlas.query --db atlas.db --out work/pair.md pair ${input:field} ${input:field2}; python -m atlas.query --db atlas.db --out work/messages.md messages ${input:pattern}; python -m atlas.query --db atlas.db --out work/field.md field ${input:field}

tasks.label: Atlas: document outline -> work/doc.md
tasks.detail: A document's sections: numbers, headings, sizes. Then read them in full with the next task.

tasks.label: Atlas: document sections about a term -> work/doc.md
tasks.detail: The FULL text of every section of one document that contains the term - what the model reads for a business rule.

tasks.label: Atlas: interfaces -> work/interfaces.md
tasks.detail: What leaves or enters the mainframe and via whom (FTP, NDM, MQ, DDF, web, TD queues), with declared peers.

tasks.label: Atlas: coverage -> work/coverage.md
tasks.detail: Read this before trusting anything: what contributed facts, what was skipped, what is missing.

tasks.label: Atlas: verify work/answer.md -> work/gate.txt
tasks.detail: The gate. Save the model's answer as work/answer.md first. FAIL means the answer is wrong; run /atlas-fix in the chat.

tasks.label: Atlas: verify the file open in the editor
tasks.detail: Same gate on whatever answer file is open.

tasks.label: Atlas: UI (fetch, build, coverage)
tasks.detail: The desktop window: sources, Fetch, Build index, Coverage, OCR images.

tasks.label: Atlas: selfcheck
tasks.detail: Run after every git pull. Must print SELFCHECK PASSED.
